issues.legal_issue: The family arrangement made a specific village separate property rather than leaving it part of an impartible estate.
material_facts: The family arrangement provided that the village would belong absolutely to the member next entitled to succeed to the estate.
The arrangement was accepted by the family members, and the village was separated from the estate and enjoyed as that member’s private property.
issues.conclusion: The village was separate property, not an integral part of the zamindari, and on the holder’s death it devolved by succession; his widow was entitled to it as his heir.
issues.legal_principle: A family arrangement accepted by the relevant family members may separate a property from an impartible estate and impress it with the character of separate property. The Court relied on the arrangement and the parties’ acceptance and conduct, and distinguished the question from whether the impartible estate itself had ceased to be joint family property.

predicates.impartible_estate_succession_dispute: The proceeding concerns succession to property associated with an impartible estate.
predicates.family_arrangement_allocated_village_abs: The family arrangement allocated a village absolutely to an individual family member.
predicates.family_members_accepted_arrangement: The family members accepted the arrangement and acted on it.

issues.definition: When a succession dispute concerning an impartible estate involves an accepted family arrangement allocating a village absolutely, the allocated village is separate property and devolves by individual succession.

issues.legal_issue: Lands and buildings conveyed absolutely to a widow under a family arrangement ceased to be part of the joint family estate and passed to her stridhana heirs.
material_facts: Under the family arrangement, the widow received the pannai lands, buildings, and movables absolutely, with power of alienation.
The member who obtained an absolute interest in the estate was competent to convey those properties to the widow.
The widow’s granddaughters succeeded to the lands as her stridhana heirs; a later release in favour of the estate holder was found by the courts below to be vitiated by fraud and inoperative.
issues.conclusion: The lands and buildings became the widow’s absolute property, ceased to be part of the joint family estate, and passed to her stridhana heirs; the widow claimant was entitled to their possession.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sartaj Kuari’s case, a holder competent to alienate property could convey the pannai lands absolutely. The Court applied the clear terms of the family arrangement and upheld the concurrent finding that the later release was vitiated by fraud.

predicates.impartible_estate_property_dispute: The proceeding concerns ownership of lands or buildings associated with an impartible estate.
predicates.competent_holder_conveyed_lands_absolute: A holder competent to convey the lands granted them to a widow absolutely under a family arrangement.
predicates.later_release_was_inoperative: A later release purporting to transfer the lands was found to be inoperative.

issues.definition: Where a competent holder conveys associated lands absolutely to a widow and a later purported release is inoperative, the lands are separate property passing to the widow’s stridhana heirs.

issues.legal_issue: A family arrangement that settles immediate possession and allocates other properties does not, without clear evidence of an intention to renounce succession, convert an impartible estate into the separate property of the current holder’s branch.
material_facts: The zamindari was an impartible estate owned by a Hindu joint family, and the junior branches could not demand its partition.

The 1890 arrangements gave the holder possession after the widow’s lifetime and allocated other properties, but did not expressly renounce the junior branches’ contingent right to succeed if the holder’s line became extinct.
Family members described the family as undivided and referred to the person next entitled to succeed; the evidence did not show a clear intention to end the joint family character of the zamindari.
The widow claimed the zamindari as the separate property of her husband, while members of other branches asserted succession through the family.
issues.conclusion: The 1890 arrangement did not prove a partition or renunciation of the junior branches’ expectancy of succession. The zamindari remained joint family property for succession purposes, and the widow’s claim to it as her husband’s separate property failed.
issues.legal_principle: To establish that an impartible estate has ceased to be joint family property for succession, the party asserting separation must prove an express or implied intention to renounce the chance of succession and to impress the estate with the character of separate property. A power to alienate an impartible estate does not imply a power to partition it. The Court relied on Konammal v. Annadana, Collector of Gorakhpur v. Ram Sundar Mal, and Sri Raja Lakshmi Devi Garu v. Sri Raja Surya Narayana, and distinguished Vadrevu Ranganayakamma, Sivagnana Tevar, and Thakurani Tara Kumari.

rule.if: impartible_estate_succession_dispute and family_members_preserved_contingent_succession and not clear_intention_to_sever_estate and holder_power_to_alienate

predicates.impartible_estate_succession_dispute: The proceeding concerns succession to an impartible estate held by a family.
predicates.family_members_preserved_contingent_succ: Family members’ statements or arrangements preserved succession rights if the current holder’s line failed.
predicates.clear_intention_to_sever_estate: The evidence clearly shows an intention to end the estate’s joint family character and make it separate property.
predicates.holder_power_to_alienate: The holder had power to alienate the impartible estate.

issues.definition: In a succession dispute over an impartible family estate, preserved contingent succession and the absence of a clear intention to sever leave the estate joint for succession, even if its holder could alienate it.

issues.legal_issue: A general release made in the context of an immediate succession dispute does not surrender a branch’s contingent right to succeed to an impartible estate unless the surrender is in favour of all family branches or their representative.
material_facts: A senior member of one branch executed a release in favour of a widow, who was not a member of the coparcenary, while the parties were settling an immediate dispute over the estate.

The release was executed when the widow was expected to retain the zamindari absolutely, but the later compromise limited her interest to her lifetime and recognized another family member as the next heir.
The terms and circumstances showed that the releasing member gave up his immediate claim to succeed, not the branch’s contingent right to succeed if the recognized holder’s line failed.
The release did not surrender the right in favour of all branches or a family head acting for them.
issues.conclusion: The release did not extinguish the third branch’s contingent right to succeed by survivorship. The senior member of that branch was entitled to succeed ahead of the rival branch and the widow.
issues.legal_principle: A member of a joint family owning an impartible estate may renounce succession for himself and his heirs, but the relinquishment must benefit all members and be made in favour of all branches or the family head representing them. General words of release are construed in light of the circumstances and matters contemplated when the release was made. The Court relied on Directors of the L. & S.W. Ry. Co. v. Richard Doddridge and Chowdhry Chintaman Singh v. Mst. Nowlukho Kunwari.

rule.if: impartible_estate_succession_dispute and release_concerned_immediate_claim and releasee_did_not_represent_all_branches and no_clear_surrender_of_contingent_succession

predicates.impartible_estate_succession_dispute: The proceeding concerns competing claims to succession to an impartible family estate.
predicates.release_concerned_immediate_claim: The release was made to settle a claim to immediate possession or succession.
predicates.releasee_did_not_represent_all_branches: The release was made in favour of a person who did not represent all branches of the family.
predicates.no_clear_surrender_of_contingent_success: The words and circumstances of the release do not clearly show an intention to surrender a branch’s contingent right to succeed.

issues.definition: In a succession dispute over an impartible family estate, a release addressing an immediate claim in favour of someone who does not represent all branches does not extinguish contingent succession absent a clear surrender of that right.
